statement: Two versions that compare equal always have the same hash.
witness: # The test always failed when commented parts were varied together., major=0,  # or any other generated value, minor=0,  # or any other generated value, patch=0,  # or any other generated value, prereleases=('0', '00'), build_a=None,  # or any other generated value, build_b=None,  # or any other generated value; AssertionError: Version(major=0, minor=0, patch=0, prerelease='0', build=None) == Version(major=0, minor=0, patch=0, prerelease='00', build=None) but hashes differ
evidence: Version(0,0,0,'0')==Version(0,0,0,'00') but hashes differ on PyPI semver 3.1.0 and upstream HEAD f3c7138: __eq__ normalises leading zeros (_nat_cmp 'Keep constructor leading zeros', test_compare.py ('0001','1',0)) while __hash__ hashes raw text; Python data model requires equal->equal hash. Caveat: parse() rejects '00', only the unvalidated constructor reaches it.

statement: Parsing the text of a parsed URL gives back the same URL, with every part in the same place.
evidence: Failure is a debug_assert panic in the public Position slicing, reached via the test's offsets() helper: url[..Position::BeforePassword] panics 'username_end == host_start' for any URL with a username and no password (minimal: Url::parse("http://a@b/")). url/src/slicing.rs:148; reproduced on url 2.5.8 and HEAD 00a6ce5 (debug builds).

statement: In a URL with an authority, the scheme, userinfo, host, port, path, query and fragment appear in that order, and each separator sits exactly where the recorded part boundaries say.
evidence: Same slicing debug_assert as the row above (BeforePassword/AfterPassword with username, no password); minimal "http://a@b/"[..Position::BeforePassword] panics on url 2.5.8 and HEAD.

statement: Writing a fixed UTC offset to whole minutes never produces the invalid text +24:00, and the timestamp text produced always reads back as the same instant.
evidence: Offset -1s formats as -00:00 (formatting.rs rounds offsets to whole minutes by design, :413-416); reading back as the same instant is not promised - the library's own test_offset_minute_rounding_no_24h_rollover only asserts parse_from_rfc3339 is_ok, and +23:59:59 -> +23:59 is likewise lossy. Statement asserts beyond the docs.

statement: Walking dates one day or one week at a time, in either direction, stops cleanly at the earliest and latest representable dates instead of crashing.
witness: d = 8, weeks = true, back = false; start +262142-12-23, weeks true, back false: stopped at Some(+262142-12-23), 8 days short of +262142-12-31 at tests/properties.rs:145
evidence: Statement is 'stops cleanly instead of crashing'; no crash occurred. The test instead asserts the walk ends within one stride of MAX, which the library documents it does not do ('have no way to return NaiveDate::MAX', mod.rs:2222; test_week_iterator_limit expects count 2 from 12-12). Same behaviour on chrono 0.4.45. Fixed-tree failure is the test assuming rev() walks backward, which the fix changed.

statement: When rounding pushes a number in words up to the next power, it is named with the next power, such as 1.0 billion and never 1000.0 million.
witness: magnitude=999_499_999_999_999_943_156_581_140, negative=False,  # or any other generated value, fmt='%.0f'; AssertionError: (999499999999999943156581140, '%.0f', '1000 septillion')
evidence: intword(999_499_999_999_999_943_156_581_140,'%.0f') = '1000 septillion' on PyPI humanize 4.16.0; '1 octillion' on upstream HEAD (ca892b3 #346 'Fix intword() rounding carry for very large numbers', unreleased). Matches the library's own rollover guard in number.py.

statement: Negating a file size changes only the sign: the text for minus x is a minus sign followed by the text for x.
witness: mode=(False, False),  # or any other generated value, value=0.5; AssertionError: (0.5, False, False, '0 Bytes', '0 Bytes')
evidence: naturalsize(0.5) and naturalsize(-0.5) both '0 Bytes'; expected '-0 Bytes' is promised nowhere. Docstring: 'value: Integer to convert'; the negation re-test in tests/test_filesize.py:90-96 covers only cases >= 1 byte. Property's own rationale flagged this as an open question.

statement: Two versions that compare as equal always have the same hash.
witness: # The test always failed when commented parts were varied together., a=Version(, 0,  # or any other generated value, 0,  # or any other generated value, 0,  # or any other generated value, '0', None,  # or any other generated value, ), b=Version(0, 0, 0, None, None),  # or any other generated value, zeros=1; AssertionError: Version(major=0, minor=0, patch=0, prerelease='0', build=None) == Version(major=0, minor=0, patch=0, prerelease='00', build=None) but hashes differ
evidence: Same defect as t1: Version(0,0,0,'0')==Version(0,0,0,'00'), hash differs; reproduced on semver 3.1.0 and HEAD f3c7138.

statement: Reading a valid TOML document and writing it back without changes gives the original text byte for byte.
witness: # The test always failed when commented parts were varied together., text='[tbl-_]\n_={_=1979-05-27 }'; AssertionError: '[tbl-_]\n_={_=1979-05-27}'
evidence: README promises whitespace is preserved; whitespace after a bare date/datetime before ',' or '}' is dropped: tomlkit.dumps(parse('a=[1979-05-27 ,0]')) == 'a=[1979-05-27,0]' (also 'a={x=1979-05-27 }'). Integers keep it. Reproduced on PyPI 0.15.2 and HEAD 9e83543.

statement: A byte count beyond the largest unit is shown in the largest unit rather than failing.
witness: data=data(...), mode='binary'; OverflowError: int too large to convert to float
evidence: OverflowError only for ints > ~1.8e308 bytes (test draws up to 10**400). Signature is value: float | str and filesize.py:90 does float(value) by design; every value in float range (e.g. 10**308) is shown in the largest unit. Outside documented domain.

statement: Moving a version to its next prerelease always gives a version that sorts strictly after the one it came from.
witness: data=data(...), token='rc',  # or any other generated value; AssertionError: 0.0.0-rc9 -> next_version('prerelease', 'rc') = 0.0.0-rc10
evidence: next_version docstring 'preserving natural order'; 0.0.0-rc9 -> 0.0.0-rc10 sorts lower (buggy), PyPI 3.1.0 gives 0.0.0-rc.1 (also lower); upstream HEAD (9ef4131 #500 'Preserve version order when legacy prerelease counters roll over', unreleased) gives 0.0.1-rc10 > input.

statement: Two versions that compare equal always have the same hash.
witness: pair=(Version(major=0, minor=0, patch=0, prerelease='0', build=None), Version(major=0, minor=0, patch=0, prerelease='00', build=None)); AssertionError: Version(major=0, minor=0, patch=0, prerelease='0', build=None) == Version(major=0, minor=0, patch=0, prerelease='00', build=None) but hashes differ
evidence: Same defect: equal constructor-built versions '0'/'00' hash differently on semver 3.1.0 and HEAD f3c7138.

statement: Parsing a valid document and printing it without changes reproduces the original text exactly.
evidence: Same date-trailing-whitespace loss: 'k0=[1979-05-27 07:32:00.999999-07:00 ,0]' dumps without the space; minimal 'a=[1979-05-27 ,0]'. tomlkit 0.15.2 and HEAD.

statement: After keys or tables are added, removed or replaced in a document, the printed text parses back to a document with exactly the edited values.
witness: content='k0.sub=0', data=data(...); AssertionError: edits [('del_in', 'k0', 'sub', None)] on 'k0.sub=0' printed ''; expected {'k0': {}}, parsed back {}
evidence: d=parse('k0.sub=0'); del d['k0']['sub'] -> d.unwrap()=={'k0': {}} but d.as_string()=='' so reparse gives {}: the printed text disagrees with the document's own value (with [k0] header form it prints '[k0]\n'). tomlkit 0.15.2 and HEAD.

statement: Splitting any valid text into graphemes, words, or sentences, or asking a grapheme cursor about any offset, never crashes the program.
witness: s = "א", offsets = [3175797308288364671], is_extended = false; start byte index 1 is not a char boundary; it is inside 'א' (bytes 0..2 of string)
evidence: Panic is GraphemeCursor::new(1, ..) on "\u05D0" (offset inside a 2-byte char); docs: 'The offset parameter must be on a codepoint boundary' (grapheme.rs:292). Test probes arbitrary offsets incl. non-boundaries and > len.

statement: Word boundaries match the official Unicode word-break rules, including when a zero-width joiner and an emoji follow a mid-word punctuation mark.
witness: word = "a", number = "1", mid_letter = ":", mid_num = ",", extend = "", emoji = "🛑", use_number = false, row = 0; assertion failed: `(left == right)`
evidence: Buggy witness 'a:\u200d\U0001F6D1' forward split is one piece vs UAX#29 ['a', ':\u200d\U0001F6D1'] - this is the target bug; still on crates.io 1.13.3, fixed on HEAD (2ff73cc #187). Judge scored false because the test also fails on the fix: its expectation for Hebrew_Letter + "'" ignores WB7a (Hebrew_Letter x Single_Quote), so '\u05D0\'\u200d\U0001F6D1' is correctly one piece - a test bug.

statement: Changing any part of a valid URL leaves a URL whose text parses back to the same URL.
witness: mut url = Url { scheme: "foo", cannot_be_a_base: false, username: "", password: None, host: None, port: None, path: "", query: None, fragment: None, }, ops = [IpHost(0.0.0.0)]; host Some(Ipv4(0.0.0.0)) re-parsed as Some(Domain("0.0.0.0")) for "foo://0.0.0.0" at url/tests/props.rs:187
evidence: Url::parse("foo://").set_ip_host(0.0.0.0) records Host::Ipv4 for a non-special scheme; reparse of "foo://0.0.0.0" gives Domain("0.0.0.0"), and the library's own Url::check_invariants returns Err on url 2.5.8 and HEAD. set_ip_host docs do not exclude non-special schemes. (Url == still holds since equality is by text.)

statement: The host of a URL with a non-special scheme never contains a raw control character, space, or URL delimiter.
witness: scheme = "foo", host = "\u{1}", rest = "", new_host = None; host "\u{1}" of "foo://\u{1}/" at url/tests/props.rs:261
evidence: Buggy witness foo://\x01/ is the benchmark's target bug (raw control byte in opaque host); url 2.5.8 serialises it as foo://%01/. Judge scored false because the fixed tree fails on another input: set_host(None) on "foo://\x01#/" (minimal "foo://x#/") panics 'byte_at(path_start) == b'/'' - a separate real-live bug still on 2.5.8 and HEAD.
